cases.name: levelOnly_endsOnBoundary
cases.note: No trend, sixteen points, four per cycle. The initialisation is exactly the fixed point here, so residuals are zero from the very first observation — nothing to converge.

cases.name: levelOnly_offBoundary_1
cases.note: One point past a cycle boundary. The forecast must start one phase further round; the old indexing returned the boundary answer.

cases.name: levelOnly_offBoundary_3
cases.note: Three points past — with the boundary case above, every residue mod the cycle length is covered.

cases.name: withTrend_quarterly
cases.note: A linear trend as well as a season. The trend must be carried into the forecast at the right rate; a model that dropped it would still look seasonal.

cases.name: withTrend_offBoundary
cases.note: Trend and season, ending mid-cycle: both defects at once.

cases.name: monthly_converged
cases.note: Twelve periods per cycle with slower smoothing (alpha 0.3, gamma 0.2), so it needs far more data to settle: the largest relative forecast error runs 1.4e-05 at n=600, 2.9e-08 at 1200, 5.1e-14 at 2400 and exactly zero at 4800. Generated at 2400, comfortably inside the assertion.

cases.name: negativeTrend
cases.note: A declining series. Nothing in the algebra prefers a positive slope, and a sign error would only show here.

name: holtWinters
note: Each series is a constant level plus a linear trend plus a fixed seasonal pattern, with no noise, so additive Holt-Winters must reproduce it exactly: residuals zero, forecasts equal to the continuation of the generating formula. `expectedForecast` is computed from that formula and never from a forecaster.
reference: exact recovery — the generating formula, not another implementation. See the module docstring for why statsmodels was tried and rejected as the oracle.
